caption:
Georgetown December closing. Snowed in?

A winter closing adds a few questions to ask early. 1) Closing near the holidays? Ask your lawyer about office hours and the deadline for your closing funds. 2) Ask your movers what happens if it snows, and get the answer in writing. 3) At the final walkthrough, run the furnace and check that the heat works. 4) Set up heat and hydro in your name before keys day. These are planning questions, not rules: your lawyer and your agreement of purchase and sale decide the details.

$500K, 30 years. Extra interest?

New Reel on my page tonight: what a 30-year mortgage can add in interest compared with 25 years, worked out on a $500,000 example. Take a guess first.

Planning a move? Comment INFO to get full details, or call 905-452-4298.

Example only. Not mortgage, tax or legal advice.

Krishna Rander, Realtor® | PROPERTY.CA INC., Brokerage

#GTArealestate #mortgagetips #keyswithkrishna

Lower monthly mortgage. Bigger catch?

Example only: a $625,000 Kitchener home with 20% down means a $500,000 mortgage. At 4.34% (interest compounded semi-annually, rate held for the whole amortization):
1) 25 years: $2,723.07 a month. 30 years: $2,474.73 a month. That is about $248 a month less.
2) Interest over 25 years: $2,723.07 x 300 - $500,000 = $316,921.
3) Interest over 30 years: $2,474.73 x 360 - $500,000 = $390,903, which is $73,982 more.
A longer amortization lowers the monthly mortgage but costs more interest over time. Whether 30 years is available depends on your lender and mortgage type, and rates change at renewal. 4.34% is an example from the lowest advertised 5-year fixed rates (insured); uninsured rates can differ. Lenders also apply the stress test and debt ratios.

caption:
Etobicoke keys today. Frozen pipes tonight?

The first winter night in a new home matters. The City of Toronto's tips: 1) Find the main water shut-off valve and make sure it works. 2) Keep areas with water pipes above 8°C, especially near the water meter. 3) Keep your home warm, including overnight and when you are away. 4) Open kitchen, bathroom and laundry cabinet doors so warm air can circulate around the plumbing. 5) If a pipe may be frozen, never use a blowtorch, propane heater or any open flame; the City says you may wish to contact a licensed plumber if you still have no water after trying to thaw it. Etobicoke is part of Toronto; if you live elsewhere, check your own city or region's advice.
Source: City of Toronto, "Prevent or Thaw Frozen Pipes" (toronto.ca, date modified Nov 17, 2026), checked Nov 25, 2026.

caption:
Missed mortgage payments: highest since 2013.

Equifax Canada's Q3 2026 report (released November 24, 2026) says the national 90+ day mortgage balance delinquency rate reached 0.32%, up 31.1% from a year earlier and the highest since Equifax began tracking it in 2013. Ontario and British Columbia accounted for 91% of the annual growth in severely delinquent mortgage accounts. Equifax's Rebecca Oakes told The Canadian Press that mortgage delinquencies overall are still under one per cent. Equifax also says fixed-rate holders are largely protected until they renew. The Bank of Canada raised its policy rate to 2.5% last month, and its next decision is December 9.
My take: if your renewal is coming up, ask your lender about your options early. That is my opinion, not advice.
Sources: Equifax Canada, "Market Pulse" Q3 2026 release via GlobeNewswire (Nov 24, 2026); The Canadian Press via Global News (Nov 24, 2026), checked Nov 25, 2026. Forecasts can change. Not financial or mortgage advice.

caption:
Buy to impress? House-poor.

A home is a place to live, not a status symbol. If the monthly mortgage, property tax, insurance, utilities and repairs take so much of your budget that little is left for everything else, that is often called being house-poor. Before you fall for the biggest, newest or most impressive home, work out what you can comfortably carry every month, and leave room for repairs and life. Your Realtor® and your lender can help you map it out.
